To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the algebraic preconditioner proposed in this work can be used in conjunction with the GMRES method to improve the rate of convergence for solving the EFIE discretized by the MoM.
the algebraic preconditioner is effective and that the preconditioning technique can be used to improve the convergence rate of the GMRES method.
the algebraic preconditioner proposed in this work is able to improve the rate of convergence for a wide range of problems, with different geometrical and physical features.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new preconditioner, which, in addition to being easy to build, is able to provide an effective improvement of the convergence rate of the GMRES algorithm, even for the most challenging cases, i.e. when the number of unknowns is very large.

the development of a simple and robust preconditioning technique for the GMRES method, based on the properties of the skew Hermitian part of Z, which has shown to be effective for a wide range of problems.

a preconditioner that exploits some properties of the skew Hermitian part of a MoM matrix, and that is easy-to-build and computationally inexpensive to use, as opposed to other preconditioners, that are based on more sophisticated techniques, such as multigrid, multilevel, and multigrid-like methods, and that require a significant amount of CPU time to set up.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the algebraic preconditioner here proposed is an efficient tool for accelerating the convergence of the GMRES method when applied to the solution, via the MoM, of the EFIE.

the proposed preconditioning strategy is a viable and promising approach to be considered when dealing with the solution of dense, large and unstructured linear systems coming out from the MoM discretization of the EFIE.
, when the number of unknowns is not very large, a simple algebraic preconditioner like the one presented in this work can be successfully employed to significantly speed up the convergence of GMRES.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a preconditioning strategy based on the skew-Hermtian part of the impedance matrix can be successfully applied to the solution process of the MoM linear systems arising from EFIE discretization, and that it is particularly effective for large and complex problems.
the skew-Hermtian part of the MoM matrix can be exploited in order to improve the performances of the GMRES iterative solver.
the proposed preconditioner can be considered as a good alternative to the well-known algebraic preconditioners, like the incomplete LU factorization and the diagonal scaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the specific problem at hand, the proposed preconditioner has been shown to be very competitive with respect to the widely adopted diagonal scaling preconditioner.

, when the skew-Hermtian part of the impedance matrix is well-conditioned and has a relatively low condition number, the algebraic preconditioner proposed here can lead to a significant reduction in the number of iterations needed by the GMRES method in order to reach a prescribed level of accuracy in the solution of the linear system of equations.
the skew-hermitean part of the matrix Z, although not necessarily symmetric positive definite, is still able to provide a good preconditioner for the GMRES method.
